name: General Health
tagline: 60 days to build the daily habits of a healthier life.
description: A neuroscience-based 60-day program to build foundational healthy habits — movement, nutrition, sleep, stress management, and connection — and turn them into an automatic, sustainable lifestyle.

phases.label: P1
phases.title: Breaking the Cycle
phases.tag: Foundation. One healthy habit at a time.
phases.vibe: The first two weeks lay the base: hydrate, move, eat real food, and sleep well. Small consistent actions repeated at the same cues begin forming automatic habits — the brain's energy-saving autopilot working for you.

phases.label: P2
phases.title: Rewiring the Brain
phases.vibe: The starter habits are sticking — now stack them. Attach new actions to established ones and add mindfulness for stress. Consistency is turning conscious effort into effortless routine.

phases.label: P3
phases.title: Building a New Identity
phases.vibe: Health is no longer a project — it's your default. Movement, good food, sleep, and calm are simply how you live. You design an environment and routine that make the healthy choice the easy one for good.

0.title: Hydrate first + intention
0.note: 500ml water on waking and one intention for the day. Hydration kickstarts metabolism and focus; intention primes the prefrontal cortex.

0.title: 30 min movement
0.note: Walk, stretch, or work out. Daily movement improves mood, sleep, and brain health more reliably than any supplement.

0.title: One whole-food meal + veg
0.note: Build a meal around protein and vegetables. Whole foods stabilize energy and reduce the cravings processed food engineers.

0.title: 10 min morning daylight
0.note: Get outside early. Morning light sets your circadian clock for better sleep and daytime energy.

0.title: 5-10 min breathing / mindfulness
0.note: Slow breathing activates the calming parasympathetic system, lowering the chronic stress that erodes health.

0.title: Connect with someone
0.note: A call, meal, or chat. Strong social bonds are one of the biggest predictors of long-term health and longevity.

0.title: Evening reflection — 3 wins
0.note: Note three things that went well. Gratitude lowers stress and reinforces the habits worth repeating.

0.title: Sleep 7-9 hrs
0.note: Consistent bed and wake times. Sleep is when the body repairs and the brain consolidates every good habit.

1.title: Hydrate + morning routine
1.note: Anchor water and light to waking. Stacking habits onto existing cues makes them stick.

1.title: Movement + a little more
1.note: Add intensity or duration. Progressive challenge keeps improving fitness and mood.

1.title: Two whole-food meals
1.note: Extend clean eating across the day. Steady blood sugar means steady energy and fewer cravings.

1.title: Stack a new healthy habit
1.note: Attach one new action to an existing one (e.g. stretch after brushing teeth). Habit stacking wires new routines fast.

1.title: 10 min mindfulness
1.note: Deepen the practice. Regular mindfulness lowers baseline stress and improves emotional control.

1.title: Meaningful connection
1.note: Invest in a relationship today. Connection buffers stress and boosts wellbeing.

1.title: Gratitude + plan tomorrow
1.note: Reflect and set up an easy win for tomorrow. Planning removes friction.

2.title: Healthy morning ritual
2.note: Water, light, movement — automatic now. A strong morning sets the whole day.

2.title: Train — your standard now
2.note: Movement is simply part of your life. Keep it varied and enjoyable so it lasts.

2.title: Eat well by default
2.note: Whole foods are your normal. Design your kitchen so the healthy choice is the easy one.

2.title: 15 min mindfulness / de-stress
2.note: Keep stress low for long-term heart and brain health.

2.title: Nurture your circle
2.note: Relationships are a cornerstone of a long, healthy life. Tend them.

2.title: Identity journal
2.note: Write as a healthy, active person. Identity keeps habits alive after day 60.

2.title: Protect sleep
2.note: Guard your foundation. Everything good is built on good sleep.

quotes: Health is built in the small choices you repeat every day.
You don't have to be extreme, just consistent.
Take care of your body — it's the only place you have to live.
Good sleep is the foundation everything else is built on.
Small habits, stacked daily, become a different life.
Whole foods, real movement, deep sleep — the boring stuff works.
Connection is as vital to health as diet and exercise.
Sixty days of good habits become who you are.
